Wrong option 3 (Classic Load Balancer): the why gives only 'previous generation, AWS recommends migrating', which is a status argument and does not name a requirement it fails (it has no Elastic IP / fixed address support, and is not the extreme-performance choice). A reader could call it merely 'worse', and it leans on availability/recommendation wording.
Wrong option 1 (ALB) why cites only a recommendation; the failing requirement is that an ALB offers no fixed IP addresses (clients use its DNS name, whose addresses change).
suggestedFix: Rewrite the whys to name the failed requirement: ALB and Classic Load Balancer nodes have no Elastic IP association, so no fixed addresses for the partner allow-list (check an AWS page, e.g. the NLB intro quote on static IP support, or the ELB features page, for a quote that ALB/CLB lack static IP).
